meta.title: Signs of Winter — Set 4
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Sentence completion and fill-in-the-blank quiz for 'Signs of Winter'.

questions.question: In France, it is winter during which month?
options: December
July
March
September
questions.explanation: The text says: 'In France it is winter in December. In New Zealand it is winter in July.'

questions.question: Vanessa and Tom are building a huge snowman by first making a large snowball.
questions.explanation: True. The story says: 'Vanessa and Tom are building a snowman. They start by making a huge snowball.'

questions.question: Pine and fir trees have green _______ that stay on them in winter.
questions.hint: Thin, pointy leaves of pine trees.
questions.explanation: Evergreen trees have needles instead of flat leaves, and they stay on the branches in winter.

questions.question: Deciduous tree branches are bare during the winter months.
questions.explanation: True. Many trees lose all their leaves in winter, making their branches bare.

questions.question: What does Earth travel around to change the seasons?
options: the sun
the moon
the North Pole
Antarctica
questions.explanation: The text explains: 'During the year, Earth travels around the sun,' which causes changes in the seasons.

questions.question: In New Zealand, it is winter during the month of _______.
questions.hint: The summer month in the Northern Hemisphere.
questions.explanation: The text states: 'In New Zealand it is winter in July' due to its location in the Southern Hemisphere.

questions.question: How is daylight in the winter season?
options: There is very little daylight, and it gets dark early
Daylight is very long and lasts all evening
There is no daylight at all during winter
Daylight starts late at night
questions.explanation: The text says: 'There is very little daylight in winter. It gets dark out early in the evening.'

questions.question: Sort these statements into True or False according to the winter facts in the text:
questions.explanation: Winter follows autumn and brings snow instead of rain. Daylight is short, bisons grow extra thick coats, and beavers eat wood bark.

questions.question: Furry animals stay through winter because their fur keeps them warm.
questions.explanation: True. The text explains: 'Animals that have a lot of fur stay during the winter. Their fur keeps them warm.'

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe where pine needles are:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Pine needles stay on branches.' This keeps pine trees green in winter.

questions.question: Why do beavers store wood logs in the water near their lodges?
options: To eat the bark during the winter
To build a wooden sled for Bobby
To make a snowman on top of it
To keep the water warm
questions.explanation: The text explains: 'They keep them in the water near their lodges. They eat the bark during the winter.'

questions.question: In the winter, Bobby likes to go _______ down snowy hills.
questions.explanation: The text mentions: 'Bobby likes to go sledding in the winter.'

questions.question: Arrange the words to show when winter comes:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Winter comes after autumn.' Autumn is the cooling season.

questions.question: Vanessa and Tom are building a wood lodge using mud in winter.
questions.explanation: False. Beavers build lodges, while Vanessa and Tom are building a snowman.

questions.question: What is the reason the American bison's coat grows extra long and thick in winter?
options: Because the winter temperature is cold
To help the bison travel around the sun
To help it hide inside a beaver lodge
To catch snowballs thrown by children
questions.explanation: The bison's coat grows thick and long to protect its body from the freezing winter temperatures.
